newsitem.title: USA: Wisconsin Energy unit fined by NRC.
newsitem.headline: Wisconsin Energy unit fined by NRC.

text.p: Wisconsin Electric Power Co, a unit of Wisconsin Energy Corp, said Wednesday that the Nuclear Regulatory Comission (NRC) fined it $325,000 for violations that occurred this summer in the operation of the Point Beach Nuclear Plant in Two Creeks, Wis.

"While at no time was the safety of the plant called into question, the cumulative nature of these incidents makes it clear we did not perform up to NRC standards or our own expectations," Dick Grigg, chief operating officer, said in a statement.

A spokesman said the NRC complaints included incidents of inattentiveness and training held in the control room, some maintenance and testing practices involving an auxiliary pump, improper dry fuel storage, and the timeliness of amendments to the license specifying the number of service water pumps needed.
He said steps have been taken to address all these areas.

"We concur with the specific recommendations by the NRC. We have initiated prompt and aggressive actions to correct the immediate concerns raised by the NRC," Grigg said. "In addition, we continue to work with industry experts and make use of other resources in a multi-faceted effort to address the underlying cause of this decline in performance."
